title: Garden and Salt Anew
premise: Ansel Quintana, a debt-bound scribe in the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers her own name and tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies foretelling the death of the mountain court's captive soul. The soul belongs to Wren, the salt-seller who once loved her and sold himself to pay her debts. To save him, Ansel must steal him back from the court beneath the mountain, betraying both guild and temple, and learn that the prophecy was written by her own future hand. In the end she rewrites the ledger at the cost of her own recorded memory, freeing Wren while choosing to be forgotten by everyone but herself.
about_author: Ada Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers in coastal port cities before turning to fiction. She writes fantasies about paperwork, devotion, and the quiet violence of contracts.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She catalogs impossible goods—bottled tides, borrowed years—for the guild that owns her debt, keeping her head down and her handwriting perfect. A salt-seller named Wren leaves a jar on her desk with no entry in any book. Emotional beat: the ache of a life lived invisibly, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Sent to restore the guild's oldest prophecy folio, she finds tonight's date and her own name inked a century ago beside a death: 'the soul beneath the mountain.' The head archivist warns her to close the book. Emotional beat: vertigo—the discovery that invisibility was always an illusion.

chapters.title: What Wren Sold
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with a flashback to their shared childhood in the salt flats. She learns Wren sold his soul to the mountain court to clear her family's debt—the very debt binding her now. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve; love revealed as the hidden engine of her whole life.

chapters.title: Terms of Service
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She petitions the guild to void the sale; they refuse, since the prophecy guarantees the court will collect. The Guildmaster offers instead a promotion: transcribe the prophecy's final page, which is blank. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth—she realizes the guild wants her complicit, not saved.

chapters.title: Down the Salt Stair
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Using a forged writ from her own ledgers, she descends the merchant stair beneath the mountain, trading memories as toll at each gate. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration; every step costs her a piece of her past, and she chooses which pieces.

chapters.title: The Court of Kept Things
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In the mountain court she finds Wren preserved as a living record, his soul bound into a ledger like one of hers. He no longer remembers her name. Emotional beat: heartbreak sharpened into defiance—she recognizes her own future in his erasure.

chapters.title: The Blank Page
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The court's Magistrate reveals the prophecy's final page can only be written by its subject: Ansel herself, a century ago, in a loop she cannot yet understand. He offers her Wren's freedom if she completes the page as written. Emotional beat: the trap closes—duty dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Ink Against the Mountain
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Climax. Instead of completing the prophecy, Ansel writes a new line—her own, unrecorded—and strikes out the death clause, burning her accumulated memory-tolls as fuel for the ink. The court shudders; the ledgers scream. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship; love against duty, finally chosen openly.

chapters.title: Garden and Salt
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, waking above ground with no memory of the mountain or the woman who freed him, only an inexplicable grief and a salt jar he feels compelled to deliver. Ansel watches him from across the market, unknown to him. Emotional beat: bittersweet cost—the rescue succeeded exactly as she paid for it.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Debt-free and forgotten by all records—including her own past self—she begins a new ledger with a single rule: nothing written here can bind anyone. Wren approaches her stall, drawn by something he can't name, and asks her name. Emotional beat: quiet hope; memory lost, love given a second chance to be chosen freely.
